_comment: Gender and form register. checks/forms.py validates every 'de X' / 'het X' in the
chapters against this file, singular and plural.
TWO TRANCHES, DIFFERENT CONFIDENCE.
* entries with no 'src': hand-seeded and individually checked. Most carry a plural.
* entries with "src": "opmaat": bulk-transcribed from De Opmaat's woordenlijst
(printed 283-289), which marks (de)/(het) on every noun. Gender only - that list
gives no plurals - so forms.py checks their articles but not their plurals.
Where both tranches had a word, the hand-checked entry won and the bulk one was dropped.
THE SOURCE CONTAINS ERRORS; see _corrections. A gender register feeding a checker that
exists to prevent wrong Dutch cannot be transcribed on trust. Every entry was put through
three checks before merging: internal duplicate conflicts, disagreement with the
hand-verified tranche, and Donaldson's suffix rules (printed 27-32). Two real errors and
one misspelling surfaced. The compound-head rule (Donaldson 7.1.3, printed 32) found no
genuine disagreements, which is the useful negative result.
Transcribing a gender register is not reproducing prose; the examples built from it must
still be our own. Compound gender follows the last element, so a compound need only be
listed when a chapter uses it with an article.
A third, tiny tranche: "src": "compound-head". These are compounds whose gender is DERIVED
from an entry already in this file by the last-element rule, listed only because a chapter
states the article in prose and the claim should be machine-checked rather than trusted.
They assert nothing the register did not already contain. No plural is given, because the
rule transfers gender and does not license inventing a plural form nobody has attested.

appartement.why: De Opmaat prints 'appartement (de)'. Wrong: het appartement. Donaldson's -ment rule (printed 27-32) makes every -ment noun neuter.

netvlies.why: De Opmaat prints 'netvlies (de)'. Wrong: het netvlies. The same page prints 'trommelvlies (het)', so the list contradicts itself.
